selected_evidence.text: CDC directly explains that coronary artery disease can weaken heart muscle over time. Coronary plaque can reduce myocardial blood supply and coronary obstruction may cause myocardial injury. This supports coronary artery disease as a possible cause of heart muscle weakening or damage. Not every patient with CAD develops myocardial injury or heart failure. NHLBI identifies chronic damage or weakening of heart muscle as a major cause of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Reduced ventricular contractile capacity can impair cardiac pumping and lead to heart failure. The relationship is a supported causal pathway particularly for HFrEF and does not imply that all heart failure develops through the same mechanism.
